editorial:
Imagine stepping back into 1939 and seeing the magic happen before the cameras even started rolling for one of the biggest movies ever made. You get to watch the legendary Vivien Leigh and Clark Gable try out different looks, hairstyles, and gowns to see what fit their characters best. It feels like you are hanging out in a dressing room with Hollywood royalty, watching them experiment with colors and makeup in bright Technicolor. The vibe is very relaxed and behind-the-scenes, giving you a rare peek at how the studio perfected the image of the Old South before a single scene was officially filmed.

What really stands out is seeing the actresses who didn't actually make the final cut, including a young Susan Hayward. It is fascinating to compare these early tests to the final movie to see why certain choices were made. While it is not a story with a plot or action, the visual detail is amazing. If you love movie history, you should definitely track this down.
endingExplained: Since this is a collection of tests and not a story, it wraps up by showing the final look choices for the main cast. You see the last few costume tweaks for the characters before the film started production. It ends with a sense of completion, showing that the studio finally found the perfect style for Scarlett and Rhett. It concludes with a thank you to the George Eastman Museum for saving these rare clips.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old Hollywood and fashion history.
